production.note: US model years. Classic.com: "Model years for Ferrari F355 Berlinetta - Manual (1994 to 1999)"; its US-market listings run from 1995 model-year cars (Atlanta, GA; Hayward, CA) to a 1998 car (Miami, FL); no 1994 US car is listed. Ferrari: "Unveiled at a dedicated client event at Fiorano in May 1994" (ferrari-f355-page). Evo: "The changeover happened for the 1996 Model Year so that Ferrari could sell the car in the US" (evo-f355; the Motronic change). The GTS and Spider are separately named cars.

body.note: Two-seat mid-engined berlinetta. The targa-topped GTS and the Spider are sold under their own names.

transmission.note: Evo panel: "Six-speed manual, six-speed single-clutch 'F1' paddle transmission, rear-wheel drive". Ferrari: "a six-speed plus reverse mechanical gearbox" (ferrari-f355-page). The F1 gearbox is an automated manual (from the 1998 model year; Classic.com lists a separate "Berlinetta - F1" market).

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 380 cv x 0.98632 = 374.8, rounded to 375 hp. Quote (ferrari.com): "The mid-rear 3496 cc 90° V8 was longitudinally mounted and punched out 380 hp, giving it a specific power output of 109 hp/l." (ferrari.com prints its cv figure as 'hp'). Evo's panel gives the same rating converted: "Power" "375bhp @ 8250rpm" (evo-f355). No separate US SAE rating was found on an opened page.

weightLb.note: Dry weight (step 4): 1,350 kg x 2.20462 = 2,976.2, rounded to 2,976 lb. Quote (Evo specification panel, Adam Towler and Yousuf Ashraf): "Weight" "1350kg (dry)  (282bhp/ton)". Evo's text: "the quoted dry weight is 1,350kg, so likely to be 1,450kg+ with a full load of fluids". No Ferrari or major-magazine curb weight was found on an opened page (two searches); ferrari.com gives no weight. carsales' 'Kerb Weight: 1353 kg' (carsales-f355-1995, database) is evidently the dry figure and was not used. Not stated to be for an optioned car; European-specification figure. Market caveat: this is a European-specification dry weight; no US curb weight was found.

provisionalNote: Production years: the first US model year is unresolved. Classic.com (a database) says "1994 to 1999" and lists US cars from 1995, but Evo says the engine-management "changeover happened for the 1996 Model Year so that Ferrari could sell the car in the US", which may mean US sales began with 1996. Weight: a European dry figure (Evo panel, step 4) in a US record. A Car and Driver road-test curb weight for a US F355 (weight step 2), or a Ferrari North America document giving the first US model year, would make this a normal record.
reviewNotes: Owner decision needed: first US model year 1995 or 1996 (see provisionalNote). If the owner has a Car and Driver F355 test panel, its curb weight should replace the dry weight (step 2 before step 4).
